**(c)** Spending multiplier \(=1/(1-0.8)=5\). Maximum output change: \(5\times$100\text{ billion}=$500\text{ billion}\). The induced change in household saving is \(MPS\times\Delta Y=0.2\times$500\text{ billion}=$100\text{ billion}\) (increase).

**(d)** Higher real output raises transactions demand for money, shifting money demand right. With money supply fixed, the nominal interest rate rises.

**(e)** Prices of previously issued bonds fall: their fixed payments are less attractive when market interest rates rise.

**(f)** (i) Demand for dollars decreases: relatively higher U.S. inflation makes U.S. goods more expensive, reducing foreign demand for U.S. exports and hence dollars. (ii) The dollar depreciates (its international value falls).

**(g)** To support the dollar, the Fed should (i) buy euros and (ii) sell dollars.
